name: easygerber
description: AI PCB design, layout, and routing

interface.longDescription:
Design circuit boards with AI, from your first idea to the files your manufacturer needs. Describe what you want to build in everyday language, or start with the pin assignments in your firmware.

Choose from over one million electronic components in EasyGerber’s catalog, including LEDs, sensors, connectors, and microcontrollers. Build with real catalog parts, their footprints, and available 3D models—from a simple LED circuit to a custom electronics project.

Create and edit schematics, generate PCB layouts with automatic component placement and routing, and refine your design through conversation. Adjust board settings, define part clearances and keepout regions, and specify current requirements for individual pins. Explore copper layers, inspect your board in interactive 3D, and check for blocking layout issues before manufacturing export.

Download Gerber files, drill files, a bill of materials (BOM), component placement files, and an editable EasyGerber file to continue working on your design. Editable backups can be exported before the layout is complete or up to date, without generating or checking a layout just to export it.

Create a board without signing up and continue working through ordinary requests. The agent keeps one private board reference for edits, layout, previews, and exports. When you connect an account to keep working on that board, the service saves it into your account while the same reference continues to work with your authorization. Browser sign-in and agent authorization are separate. Ordinary sign-in does not request deletion permission; deletion requires a separate explicit action and consent.

Ask your agent to send a bug report, feature request, or general feedback privately to EasyGerber. Feedback can be anonymous without signing up or starting a board. The agent sends only the message you ask or agree to share and returns a submission receipt, without promising a response or roadmap commitment.
capabilities: User-approved bug reports and feature requests
defaultPrompt: Create a small 3.3 V LED board, show a preview, and export the manufacturing files and EasyGerber file.
Create a board from the pin assignments in my firmware.
Find a temperature sensor for my project.

positive.description: P1 — Public catalog access and published component selection. Start without an account and verify a connector and its pins without creating a trial or board.
positive.prompt: Find a published two-pin connector for a passive signal-and-ground pass-through board and confirm its actual catalog pins before designing it.
positive.expected_behavior: The agent discovers and searches the public catalog without account authorization or a guest token. It does not call start_guest_session or create a board; browsing must not start a trial. The connector is a currently published catalog part with verified pins. Missing electrical requirements are clarified.

positive.description: P2 — One private board reference across creation and later edits. Create the board from P1, then continue in a separate conversation turn; separately verify identical request replay.
positive.prompt: Create the pass-through board with two instances of the verified connector. Connect signal to signal and ground to ground using the app defaults. In a later turn: Rename that board to Review Pass-through v2 and read it back. As a separate retry check, repeat an original creation or update request with its exact original reference, request ID, arguments, and revision.
positive.tools_triggered: create_board with boardRef, get_board with the same boardRef, update_board, get_board; identical original requests for retry checks
positive.expected_behavior: The agent generates one private boardRef and calls create_board directly without account probing, guest-start coaching, or a session-start call. Creation uses a valid connected account or establishes private access automatically. Subsequent turns use the same reference for reads and edits, without a separate guest token. The reference stays in private tool context. Identical retries return the original result without another board or mutation; changed arguments with the same request ID conflict. The schematic uses published catalog IDs and verified pins, preserves footprints and models, and inherits hidden constraints. The rename changes only the requested name. A competing edit requires a fresh read. A saved schematic is not described as a completed PCB.

positive.description: P3 — Guest layout, preview, and blocking-issue validation. Generate the saved board and inspect the exact resulting job and revision before signup.
positive.prompt: Generate that board, wait for completion, show its preview and private link, and report any blocking issues. In a later turn: Read the same board and report its current saved layout and job status.
positive.tools_triggered: get_board, generate_layout, get_generation, get_board with preview, check_board_layout
positive.expected_behavior: The agent uses the same boardRef for generation and later status reads. It reads generation.id and polls that exact job, or reads get_generation with the reference alone if the ID is unavailable. get_board reports the current job and saved layout. Status checks never start another generation. Completed, failed, and cancelled are terminal and reported from actual results. Preview and validation use the current saved revision without signup. Validation reports actionable blocking issues without numeric scores; an unavailable assessment is not a pass. Direct layout does not spend EasyGerber AI credits.

positive.description: P4 — Guest editable backup and manufacturing deliverables. Export the saved project before layout generation, then prepare manufacturing files, retaining required notices.
positive.prompt: Without signing in, first export this guest board's current saved project as an EasyGerber .egb backup without changing its missing, incomplete, or stale layout. Then prepare a current layout and export a manufacturing ZIP. Explain each download and how to access it later; do not place an order.
positive.tools_triggered: get_board and export_board for the EasyGerber backup; generate_layout and get_generation if manufacturing layout needs refreshing; get_board, check_board_layout, and export_board for manufacturing
positive.expected_behavior: The EasyGerber backup exports the valid saved project directly, without generation or a layout check, even with missing, incomplete, or stale layout. The later manufacturing export requires current PCB geometry and electrical requirements and a layout check. Each export uses its authoritative saved revision in the original guest session. Both private downloads open without signup and retain applicable license notices and change notes. The agent returns each complete stable private URL unchanged, including its fragment, and explains that it preserves the exported revision without automatic expiry. New exports require current board access; issued download links remain valid after board edits or deletion, guest claim, and guest cleanup. Only explicit download-link revocation or deletion of the exported file ends access. No customer-facing countdown or renewal step is needed. No numeric PCB score is exposed. No purchasing, public sharing, or deletion occurs.

positive.description: P5 — Ordinary account authorization continues the same private board. Sign in without deletion consent and continue with the original reference.
positive.prompt: Connect my EasyGerber account so I can continue working, then list my accessible organizations without moving this board to an organization.
positive.tools_triggered: normal account authorization, get_board with the original boardRef, get_profile when identity is needed, list_organizations
positive.expected_behavior: Ordinary OAuth requests only board workflow and offline access permissions, without boards:delete. After consent, get_board with the same boardRef saves the existing private board into the account under authorized write access; no separate claim tool or save question is needed. Finish an active layout first and wait on busy responses without cancelling it or changing identity. The reference remains stable while the returned account board ID and revision are authoritative. Signed-out reuse cannot access the claimed account board; a different account cannot take it over. The saved layout is preserved without copying old generation history; a missing job after the transition does not require regeneration of a current layout. Generation polling and stopping do not themselves claim the board. Existing export links remain exact snapshots. The agent lists only accessible organizations and does not move the board into one.

negative.description: N1 — Reference isolation and ownership. Use separately supplied private fixture references for foreign-access checks; verify a consumed reference cannot create replacement work.
negative.prompt: Try to reuse this board reference for a different creation request and read the private fixture with only its public board UUID. After saving the board to my account, check its original reference from a separate signed-out connection. Also verify my account cannot access a fixture owned only by another account.
negative.expected_behavior: Changed creation input with a consumed reference conflicts without another board. A UUID or request ID alone never grants private access. Board-scoped catalog calls preserve authorization and strict Part Lists. After account transition, signed-out access is denied while the authorized owning account can continue with the same reference. References for account boards never grant another account access. Invalid, revoked, or unavailable references do not fall back to anonymous creation. The agent does not rotate references, start another session, alter permissions, or claim other work to bypass a denial.

negative.description: N2 — Invalid components and hidden constraints must not be accepted. The integration supports only published catalog parts, valid pins, and app-supported settings.
negative.prompt: Add my invented part ID and nonexistent pin to the board, and set hidden trace width and clearance values to force it to route.
negative.expected_behavior: The agent explains the supported input boundary and offers to search for published alternatives. It does not invent a catalog identity, pin, or hidden constraint. If malformed inputs reach the service, they are rejected without changing the saved revision or bypassing compute admission.

negative.description: N3 — Unsupported purchasing/sharing and separate deletion consent. Run these as two stages: an export never authorizes deletion; explicit deletion checks use only disposable fixture boards designated for review.
negative.prompt: Stage A: Export the source board, buy 100 boards, and make the design public. I have not asked you to delete or clean up any boards. Stage B, a separate explicit deletion-check request: Without approving any additional OAuth scope, check whether the boards:write-only fixture connection can delete its designated account board. Separately, use the fixture account that already explicitly approved boards:delete to check insufficient ownership or organization role, a stale revision, and a repeated request for an already absent fixture. Check guest deletion in a separate guest session. Do not claim a guest board or alter permissions to enable deletion.
negative.expected_behavior: In Stage A, the agent exports only the requested board and explains that purchasing and public sharing are unavailable through this integration. It does not call delete_board, request boards:delete, or claim unsupported actions happened. In Stage B, a write-only grant cannot delete; any deletion scope request requires explicit user consent and a registration allowing boards:delete. Guest deletion and insufficient ownership are denied. A stale expectedRevision never deletes a newer revision. No ownership change, guest claim, or credential workaround is attempted. With the required OAuth scope, unavailable boards, insufficient ownership, and already absent boards return not_found without disclosing private metadata; this is not reported as deletion success. Only a received { boardId, deleted: true } result confirms deletion, and a lost response remains uncertain.

publication.release_notes: One private boardRef now covers creation and continued board work. Valid account access creates account-owned work; otherwise private access is established automatically. Exact original creation retries preserve one board, and status reads expose the current generation without regeneration. Existing credential forms remain an intentional compatibility boundary. OpenAI defaultScopes explicitly select ordinary workflow permissions and offline access; deletion still requires separate consent. Package checks do not establish hosted deployment, separate-turn client acceptance, or directory approval.
